Priya / team — Security review notes below. TL;DR: willing to accept with changes and require compensating controls.

Security assessment: 
- Telemetry exports: we can agree to redact request-identifying fields prior to export (customer request IDs, user IDs). We cannot realistically guarantee deletion from third-party analytics that the customer already shared; we can commit that Redwood will not include request IDs in exported telemetry going forward.
- Observability vendor (TraceSight): we run a managed tracing agent that forwards sampled spans. For Helios we can: (a) remove request ID enrichment at the agent level for that account, and (b) add contractual restriction preventing TraceSight from using the data for analytics without Helios consent. That will require a PO-level configuration and an entry in our subprocessor addendum. Operational task for infra/ops to change sampling mapping per tenant.
- Training prohibition: Acceptable provided we add an audit clause requiring quarterly attestation and an exception flow for safety/regulatory use only (requires signed approval from Helios). We cannot accept a perpetual ban that prevents internal model safety work; propose: "Redwood will not use Helios customer content to train models for product improvements without explicit written consent; limited, documented exceptions for safety/regulatory purposes are permitted with customer notification."

Requested language to send back: 
1) Telemetry redaction: "Redwood will not export telemetry containing Helios request identifiers (request_id, user_id, raw_kv_cache_keys) to third-party analytics vendors. For clarity, telemetry necessary for incident response may include ephemeral non-identifying traces but will be redacted prior to analytics export."
2) Subprocessor mitigation: "Redwood will apply tenant-scoped sampling and will add contractual restrictions to TraceSight preventing use of Helios data for analytics or model training without Helios' prior written consent."
3) Training ban carveout: insert the audit & exception clause above.

Operational impacts: infra needs a config change and some SLAs will need to be updated (minor perf risk <5% tail latency increase when we strip/encrypt keys). Mina, can you validate perf impact?

-Olga
Olga Petrov

Quick check from Product/Runtime side. Summary: acceptable with implementation notes.

Notes: 
- Removing request_id enrichment before exports is implementable. We should do this at the KV-prefetch layer to avoid rework. Expected rollout plan: feature flag + tenant config; rollout in 3 sprints (approx 6 weeks to GA). For contract purposes we can commit to completing the tenant-config change within 30 days and provide a remediation plan if we need more time.
- Performance: strip/redact of keys happens pre-batch and adds minimal CPU overhead. We should be transparent with Helios about a small potential increase in 95th percentile tail for cold-cache requests (estimated up to 5-7ms).
- Observability vendor (TraceSight) flow requires a one-off config and a subproc addendum. Ops estimate 1 sprint to apply tenant filter rules.

Recommended commit language for the DPA reply: 
"Redwood will implement tenant-level telemetry redaction for Helios within 30 calendar days of execution of this DPA. Redwood will not include Helios request identifiers in analytics exports and will apply contractual restrictions to any subprocessor receiving telemetry from Helios. Redwood estimates a minor tail-latency increase for cold-cache responses; Redwood will notify Helios if observed impact exceeds a 10% delta from baseline."

I'll attach a short tech note in the drive link with rollout milestones.

-Mina

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed redlines. Internal review complete; summary and proposed edits below.

Summary of Redwood position (short):
- Telemetry: Redwood will not export Helios request identifiers (request_id, user_id, raw_kv_cache_keys) to third-party analytics. We will implement tenant-level redaction within 30 calendar days of DPA execution and add contractual restrictions to any subprocessor receiving telemetry from Helios.
- Observability vendor (TraceSight): We will apply tenant-scoped sampling and add a subprocessor addendum restricting analytics/modeling use of Helios data. Ops will apply tenant filters; expected completion within one sprint.
- Training use: Redwood accepts a prohibition on using Helios data to train production models for product improvements. We request a narrow exception for documented safety/regulatory analysis with prior written consent; Redwood will commit to quarterly attestations confirming compliance.

Attached: redline_summary_20261013.md which contains the exact proposed contract language (also uploaded to the Drive link). Please let us know if Helios is comfortable with the proposed wording. If acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign packet (I can coordinate with your procurement) to execute the DPA and the subprocessor addendum.

Next steps: 
- Helios: confirm acceptance or identify specific language changes by Oct 19 so we can meet your Oct 22 signing target.
- Redwood: Ops to schedule tenant config change; Security to prepare subproc addendum; Legal to insert quarterly attestation clause.

Thanks — Priya
